name: Pitta Pitta
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: Place primary stress on the first syllable of every word, and secondary stress on the first syllable of every polysyllabic morpheme that is not the first. if a non-initial polysyllabic morpheme is preceded by a monosyllabic morpheme, the stress may be optionally advanced to this monosyllable. Secondary stress falls on alternates, but not on the last (Blake & Green 1971:32)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict, word-initial primary stress) rests on Blake 1979, the standard reference sketch by the language's principal describer, held as an open ANU PDF, with the deciding passage confirmed verbatim on printed p.191. The StressTyp2 passages (Blake & Breen 1971:32; Hayes 1995:201) are confirmed in the on-file SQL dump and agree: primary stress initial, secondary on the third syllable of quadrisyllables with morphological conditioning in longer words. The language is extinct; Glottolog lists no phonology or instrumental work, and Roth 1897 (downloaded now) gives no rule. Nothing suggests the classification is wrong. sources.quote: "Each word pronounced in isolation is marked by a stress on the initial syllable. The remaining syllables of a disyllabic or trisyllabic word are not as weak as unstressed syllables are in English. ... In words of more than two syllables, there is a tendency for a secondary stress to appear. It normally appears on the third syllable of words of four syllables. In a word of five syllables where a new morpheme begins in the fourth syllable, the secondary stress appears in the fourth syllable, taku

sources.quote: No general stress rule. Sect.3: 'the component syllables, accentuation, &c., of all words noted as being used in the Boulia District are described in the Pitta-Pitta vocabulary, which should be freely consulted (sect. 44)'; sect.43: 'All words are analysed into their component syllables, and accentuated and pronounced according to the basis laid down in section 3.' Accent is marked per word in the vocabulary only.

sources.note: Primary source of the StressTyp2 rule our database quote rests on (p.32: morpheme-initial secondary stress, optional advancement onto a preceding monosyllabic morpheme, alternating secondaries never final); the fullest description of the language (192 pp. vs the 61-pp. HAL sketch). Would let us verify passage 1631 first-hand and pin the secondary-stress pattern strings (10100 vs 10010 for 5-syllable words depends on morphology); does not threaten the fixed: initial syllable primary coding.
